item: R144(b) stuck-lock detector for the settings hold; the table doors of the worker-only rows pinned
summary: A settings save or a restore's hold that meets kv_store._hold_lock owned by a thread that is in none of the code that takes it (or by a dead thread) is refused with KvLockStuck (a KvWriteRefused: the same 503) naming operation, thread kind and UTC time, never a thread name, and never replacing the lock; no timeout and no number: where the owner is decides, on two looks. Residuals stated in the code. Probed with real interrupts before and after: 0 left held and 0 leaked on 28,593 and 30,759 write-slot interrupts, 0 on 82,281 and 82,292 restore-hold interrupts; about +3.1 us per save. Five mutants each red. tests/test_registry_doors_pinned.py pins the callers of registry.run_all_bounded, registry.run_all (no caller outside the tests) and diagnostics_slots.members, the only doors into two loops the reach tool called UNKNOWN.
